free_tier.stated: No published byte quota on the site pages read. A 2020 project commit records an 81 MB artifact rejected as 'too large for clojars', and a later commit adds a client-side size guard. There is a per-artifact ceiling historically around 100 MB. Treat the cap as approximately 100 MB and unverified.

retention.stated: per-object-cap: ~100 MB, from third-party evidence only (81 MB jar rejected). retention: indefinite (Maven-layout artifacts are immutable once deployed)

egress.terms: Free. repo.clojars.org is S3/CloudFront-backed ('Server: ... NoSuchKey' XML errors expose S3 origin) and serves without metering.

record.tooling: `lein deploy clojars`, `clj -T:build deploy` / deps-deploy, `mvn deploy` with the clojars repo, and plain HTTPS/Maven layout GETs. No rclone backend.
record.chaining: unlimited artifacts (group/artifact/version) x unlimited versions x unlimited Clojars accounts (signup with an SSH key, free). At ~100 MB/artifact that is 100 MB x N; 20 TiB would need ~200,000 artifacts. Trivially repeatable in principle, brutally inefficient.
record.limits_note: per-object-cap: ~100 MB, from third-party evidence only (81 MB jar rejected). retention: indefinite (Maven-layout artifacts are immutable once deployed). request-rate: not documented. Write path is authenticated `lein deploy` with a Clojars token.
record.reliability_note: Read path serves real jars (verified 3,224 and 16,324 bytes on real artifacts). The cap is the story and it is poorly documented - the only hard numbers come from a 2020 project commit and forum traffic. Confirming the current number would need an authenticated deploy probe.

evidence.proved: 'the uberjar task produced an 81MB jar file which was too large for clojars'

record.notes: No published byte quota on the site pages read. A 2020 project commit records an 81 MB artifact rejected as 'too large for clojars', and a later commit adds a client-side size guard. There is a per-artifact ceiling historically around 100 MB. Treat the cap as approximately 100 MB and unverified.

dead_end.why: No published byte quota on the site pages read. A 2020-era project commit records an 81 MB uberjar being rejected as 'too large for clojars', and a later commit adds a client-side 'uberjar size guard' - so there is a per-artifact ceiling in the tens-of-MB, historically around 100 MB.
